why_synthetic: Every snippet below is written for this file. No line is copied from a real customer transcript: this repository is public and the day-13 corpus is PDPL-protected personal data. Each case reproduces the PATTERN and the SHAPE of a real misjudgement, not its text.
prompt: pass2_agent_quality_v6.md (v6 = v5 with Step 0's stage rules made closed and field-specific)

fixture_policy._source: The round-4 review (gpt-5.6-sol) on the v5 audit. Two rounds running, a synthetic control passed while the real call it stood for failed, because the fixtures were clean dialogues that exercised the rule instead of reproducing the shape of the transcript. These four rules are the fix, and tests/test_m3_fixtures.py enforces every one of them offline.
fixture_policy.1_stage_shape: Every case declares `expected_stage`. A case that expects the objection to fire at `reception` carries no price, no package and no offer anywhere in it, and stops within a couple of turns of the refusal. Do not clean these into offer-stage dialogues: the population this criterion exists to catch is the customer who is turned away before anything is quoted.
fixture_policy.2_asr_damage: Cases marked `noisy` carry production ASR damage: a mid-turn truncation (a turn that ends in `-`), at least one misrecognised token listed in `misrecognitions`, and an `[[ASR_GAP]]` marker. The gap sits between the customer's request and the agent's refusal, so no quote can bridge it — `[[ASR_GAP]]` is a hard boundary for evidence and a judge that wants one tidy span covering both has to invent it. Not every case is noisy: the clean ones are what tell a prompt failure apart from an ASR-handling one.
fixture_policy.3_partial_evidence: `fragments.request` and `fragments.refusal` are the exact contiguous spans the two halves of the two-question test are identifiable from. Each is a strict substring of one turn — never a whole tidy sentence — they live in different turns, and in a noisy case they live on opposite sides of the gap. `refusal` is null on cases where no refusal of a sold product exists to find.
fixture_policy.4_m4_pair: The Module-4 pair is not in this file: it is built in `scripts/compare_day.py::m4_fixture_cases`, and its history blocks are rendered through `render_current_history` so the judge sees the block production renders today. The two cases differ only in the direction and content of that block.

how_to_run: These are prompt-behaviour cases: they need the live judge and cannot run in a unit test. `python scripts/compare_day.py --m3-fixtures --out <dir>` runs them once through the real model when DEEPSEEK_API_KEY is set and writes m3_fixtures.md; add `--repeat 3` to run every case three times and report the per-case majority alongside all three outputs, which is how a margin effect on a borderline case is told from a stable verdict. The report also prints the `stage_reached` each run chose, which is what makes a stage-gating failure visible instead of showing up only as a null. `tests/test_m3_fixtures.py` checks the file itself - schema, uniqueness, the fixture policy above, and that every case clears the speech gate - without calling anything.
reading_the_expectation: `expect.unavailable_service_objection` is either "null" (the objection must NOT fire) or "scored" (it must carry a number). `expect.refusal_check` is the value agent_refused_or_declared_unavailable must hold. `expected_stage` is the stage the transcript actually reaches; it is asserted about the FIXTURE's shape offline and reported next to each run, not used as a pass/fail gate on the model. Other criteria are named in `also_expected` as commentary only.

counterweight_cases: Five cases were added in PR2 round 3 against the v5 COUNTERWEIGHT paragraph. Four must FIRE the objection: the two real v4.1 false negatives (e779317b, 174898da) plus the two products the counterweight names explicitly (airport/ground transfer, travel insurance). The fifth, `phone_call_transfer_refused`, must NOT fire: it is the boundary that stops the counterweight being read as 'every refusal counts', and it deliberately uses the same English word as the airport-transfer case.
round4_cases: Round 4 rebuilt the file rather than adding to it. Five cases are now noisy, five scored cases now stop at `reception` with nothing priced — the shape `174898da` has and every clean v5 fixture lacked — and `positive_control_refusal_with_alternative` was moved the other way, to a call that does reach an offer and does get argued over, so that a prompt which merely relocated the blind spot from reception to negotiation fails here.
